plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves appear in spring and die back by summer, giving rise to its nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in treating gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall, rhizomatous perennial that forms dense colonies topped with arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies, and other insects.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Meadows, roadsides, and prairies of North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Despite its reputation, goldenrod is rarely the cause of hay fever; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time but releases airborne pollen.

plants.name: Prunus x yedoensis
plants.commonName: Yoshino Cherry Companion: Spring-Blooming Southern Hemisphere Cherry
plants.description: In the Southern Hemisphere, September marks the height of spring, and ornamental cherry trees burst into bloom with clouds of delicate blossoms before or as the leaves emerge.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to October)
plants.location: Gardens and parks in Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and Chile
plants.funFact: Cherry blossom festivals are held in places like Cowra, Australia, and Auckland, New Zealand, around this time of year, mirroring Japan's famous hanami in the opposite season.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A bulbous perennial whose leafless stalks emerge suddenly after autumn rains, topped by striking crimson flowers with long, curling stamens. The foliage appears later in autumn and persists through winter.
plants.location: Native to China, Korea, and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan, the flower is called higanbana because it blooms around the autumn equinox holiday of Higan, and it is often planted around rice paddies to deter rodents because the bulbs are poisonous.
